validation.name: tiny tiling parity: released VAE structure at a small width vs diffusers after enable_tiling(...), float32

metrics.note: latent sizes 7, 10 and 11 are not multiples of the stride 3, so every grid has partial edge tiles

validation.criterion: rel_max <= 1e-4 for every case; blend_v/h/t bit-exact; tiled differs from untiled (guard)

validation.name: stage B: real Lite-distill VAE, MLX float32 with the reference default tiling vs diffusers float32 on CPU after enable_tiling(), first 8 latent frames of real Baseline latents (480x864, from an MLX bf16 generation, seed 42)

metrics.tiles: 3 temporal tiles (the last partial) x 15 spatial tiles

validation.criterion: PSNR >= 40 dB vs the reference tiled decode; peak memory recorded

validation.name: validation run: scripts/generate.py --preset baseline (480x864, 121 frames, 10 steps, seed 42, bf16 DiT, the study notebook's orbit_woman baseline prompt)

metrics.visual: follows the prompt (foreground column passes early, the camera reaches the rear three-quarter view); no tile seams visible

deviations.what: stage B compares the first 8 of 31 Baseline latent frames (29 of 121 output frames), not the whole clip
deviations.why: the torch CPU float32 reference peaks at 40.6 GiB per temporal tile on this 48 GB Mac and needs about 4 minutes per temporal tile (about 44 minutes for all 11), with a real risk of filling the disk with swap as on earlier runs. The 8-frame input exercises every tiling path (a full 3 x 5 spatial grid with partial edge tiles, temporal blending, a partial last temporal tile); the MLX and torch decodes get the same input. The whole clip can be recorded later on a machine with more memory or with --device mps.

deviations.what: Baseline is 480x864, 121 frames, not 512x768 as in the spec's goal
deviations.why: the pipeline's Baseline preset (spec 09) and the study notebook's Baseline profile use 480x864; 512x768 would need a different DiT run and is not used anywhere in the project

deviations.what: Baseline latents for stage B come from an MLX generation, not a diffusers run
deviations.why: a diffusers Baseline run would take hours on CPU; the decoder parity only needs realistic latents given identically to both decoders

deviations.what: public API additions: decode(..., callback=...), num_tiles, PipelineOutput.latents, __call__(vae_tiling=, progress=, on_latents=)
deviations.why: progress bars (owner's request), keeping the latents when decoding fails (a Baseline run was lost to a memory-guard stop), and stage B inputs; existing signatures and defaults are unchanged

follow_ups: Record the whole-clip Baseline reference (31 latent frames) on a larger machine or with --device mps, and add it to the stage B test.
16 GB profile (spec 14): the tiled Baseline decode peaks at 13 GB; lower the conv chunk budget and measure.
Baseline DiT speed (79 s/step, 13 min per video) is the dominant cost; spec 14.

architecture_notes.topic: decode memory no longer depends on video size
architecture_notes.note: With the reference tiling each tile is 17 frames x 256 x 256 output pixels, so the decode peaks at 12.5-13 GB for Baseline (121 x 480 x 864) versus 20.3 GB for the untiled-spatial Smoke decode (25 x 256 x 432). The remaining peak is one tile's activations at 128 channels plus mx.conv3d's chunked temporary buffers (1 GiB budget).
architecture_notes.optimization: For the 16 GB profile, lower HunyuanVideoCausalConv3d.chunk_bytes and measure; smaller tiles would change the output (per-tile GroupNorm), larger chunks would not.

architecture_notes.note: Tiles of 256 px with stride 192 decode (256/192)^2 = 1.78x the pixels, and temporal tiles of 17 output frames with stride 12 another ~1.4x: about 2.5x the work of one pass. Baseline decodes 165 tiles in 225 s (1.36 s per tile).
architecture_notes.optimization: Parity forbids changing tile sizes; batching several spatial tiles of one temporal tile into one call (same shapes) could improve GPU utilization.

architecture_notes.topic: torch CPU vs MLX for the tiled decode
architecture_notes.note: One temporal tile (15 spatial tiles) takes 238 s and 40.6 GiB RSS in torch float32 on the M3 Max CPU; MLX decodes three in 50 s at 12.5 GiB.
architecture_notes.optimization: None for the port; for references use MPS or bigger machines.

architecture_notes.note: Denoising 794 s (79 s/step for 50 220 video tokens), video decode 225 s, audio 1.6 s: the DiT is 78% of a Baseline generation.
architecture_notes.optimization: Spec 14: attention and DiT block speed first.
